context_text: ANTHROPIC, NVIDIA CRACK $1M: A pair of top AI stakeholders have reached a new milestone as the industry continues to build out its presence on K Street: the first seven-figure quarterly lobbying spend. Anthropic , the company behind AI chatbot Claude, just barely cracked the $1 million mark during Q3, according to disclosures filed this week.

— Anthropic’s $1.01 million in spending last quarter — up from $920,000 in Q2 — coincided with the White House’s unveiling of its highly anticipated AI Action Plan (and Anthropic’s offer to sell government access to its chatbot for just $1 per year). Anthropic closed out the quarter with a D.C. lobbying blitz by CEO Dario Amodei and co-founder and policy chief Jack Clark , who promised an even greater presence in the capital.

— Over the last week, however, simmering tensions between Anthropic and the White House finally spilled into public , with crypto czar David Sacks accusing the firm of running “a sophisticated regulatory capture strategy based on fear-mongering.”

— Anthropic wasn’t the only burgeoning lobbying force to cross the $1 million threshold for the first time last quarter. Semiconductor manufacturer NVIDIA blew past the milestone, with $1.9 million in lobbying expenditures in Q3. That’s compared to just $80,000 during the same time a year ago, and is triple what NVIDIA spent during Q2.

— One of Anthropic’s main competitors, ChatGPT developer OpenAI , has yet to break the seven figure mark. OpenAI spent $920,000 lobbying Washington last quarter, which was still a record for the K Street newcomer.

— The lobbying outlays by Anthropic and OpenAI last quarter, while significant, still lag behind those of established tech titans like Meta (which spent $5.8 million in Q3), Amazon (which spent $4.4 million), Google ($3.6 million), Apple ($2.5 million) and Microsoft ($2 million). But NVIDIA’s ramped up spending is already more in line with the industry. NVIDIA even outspent fellow chipmakers Intel and Qualcomm in Q3.

HILLSTAFFER ADDS RADANOVICH: HillStaffer has hired former Rep. George Radanovich , adding the eight-term member and one-time winemaker as a senior adviser at the firm.

— The Republican has been an active consultant in California politics since leaving Congress and previously spent three years as president of the California Fresh Fruit Association , representing fruit growers and shippers in Sacramento and Washington.

— His “deep understanding of multi-level government relations enhances our expertise in manufacturing & chemicals, agriculture, healthcare and financial services,” HillStaffer president Thomas Rosenfield said in a statement.

— Radanovich also had the distinction of being the first winemaker to serve in Congress since Thomas Jefferson, co-founding the Congressional Wine Caucus in 1999. Radanovich Winery opened in 1986 and remained in operation following Radanovich’s election to Congress. He closed the winery in 2003, citing poor economic conditions for California winegrowers.

context_text: — Each of the senators serves as ranking member on a committee with jurisdiction over federal lands, buildings or government ethics. KILLING HIM SOFTLY: Pras Michel, founding member of 90s hip-hop trio The Fugees, was sentenced to 14 years in prison today following a conviction on charges that he acted as an unregistered foreign agent of China, made illegal campaign contributions using foreign money and later tried to cover it up.

— Jurors convicted Michel, 52, in 2023 on 10 felony counts related to two schemes hatched by Michel and a Malaysian businessman, Jho Low , who is separately accused of embezzling billions of dollars from that country’s sovereign wealth fund.

— Michel’s trial was punctuated by testimony from star witnesses Leonardo DiCaprio , Jeff Sessions and Michel himself. Jurors heard details of the schemes, carried out by Michel and others and funded by Low, who used the billions he allegedly stole from Malaysia’s 1MDB fund to lead a glamorous lifestyle, praying with celebrities around the globe. Low used some of the money he allegedly stole to fund Hollywood films, including DiCaprio’s Wolf of Wall Street.

— Michel’s trial was punctuated by testimony from star witnesses Leonardo DiCaprio , Jeff Sessions and Michel himself. Jurors heard details of the schemes, carried out by Michel and others and funded by Low, who used the billions he allegedly stole from Malaysia’s 1MDB fund to lead a glamorous lifestyle, praying with celebrities around the globe. Low used some of the money he allegedly stole to fund Hollywood films, including DiCaprio’s Wolf of Wall Street.

— The first scheme involved an attempt to secure a meeting between Low and President Barack Obama so Low could get a picture of himself shaking the president’s hand. Michel, using money obtained from Low, donated nearly $2 million to a super PAC supporting Obama’s 2012 reelection campaign and hid the source of the money using a network of straw donors.

— The second scheme involved efforts by Michel, Republican fundraiser Elliott Broidy and others to lobby the first Trump Justice Department to drop an ongoing investigation into Low related to the 1MDB scandal. Low was indicted along with Michel but remains a fugitive in China.

— In addition to pushing for the DOJ to drop its investigation of Low, Michel and Broidy also took money from Low to lobby the Trump administration on behalf of China, pushing for officials to extradite a Chinese dissident living in New York. That dissident, Guo Wengui , was later arrested and convicted in his own fraud case. He has not yet been sentenced.

— “The sentence reflects the gravity of the defendant’s efforts to manipulate decision-making at the highest levels of our government, for profit and on behalf of foreign interests,” said John Keller , a former prosecutor on the case who resigned in February when he was ordered to dismiss the case against New York Mayor Eric Adams.
— Erica Dumas , a spokesperson for Michel, told PI “this is not the end of [Michel’s] story. He appreciates the outpouring of support as he approaches the next chapter.”

— In delivering the sentence, U.S. District Judge Colleen Kollar-Kotelly said that Michel was “dishonest in some of his answers” when he testified in his own defense during trial and that his demeanor “came across as arrogant.”
— “If this case, these facts, were presented to the government today, they would not be pursuing a FARA case against Mr. Michel,” defense lawyer Peter Zeidenberg argued.

— “One thing on which I think the defense is mistaken is the conclusion that the department does not bring FARA cases anymore,” prosecutor Sean Mulryne said, pointing at the ongoing FARA trial of former New York political aide Linda Sun .

— In belated FARA filings submitted after his guilty plea, Bendler detailed work he did for foreign principals in Venezuela, Lebanon, Angola and France as a BGR contractor, earning $6,000 per job, plus travel reimbursements.

— Bendler’s lawyer, Jesse Binnall , said that for decades, “Dale Bendler served this nation with honor, first as a United States Marine and later as a CIA officer. He has sacrificed for his country throughout his entire career and that record of service matters. Mr. Bendler’s story is not over.”

JOURNEY TO THE MANOSPHERE: The 2024 elections shined a spotlight on the widening political gap between men and women, vaulting terms like “manosphere” into the popular lexicon. And as Democrats have scrambled to find their way out of the political wilderness — in large part by trying to boost the party’s appeal to men — the progressive consultancy Precision Strategies is out with new research it hopes can help.
— In partnership with Tunnl , Precision has developed the “Manosphere Index” to provide campaigns and brands with insight into how to reach men by diving into what is shaping their worldview.

— Post-2024, “there was a lot of data and framing that very narrowly talked about this ‘masculinity crisis,’” said Krishana Davis, who leads Precision’s digital and multicultural engagement efforts. But much of that dialogue was “flattening the conversation, and basically looking at millions of men from a very monolithic view.” Or, she argued, it became “a shorthand of white men, when even white men are not a monolith.”

— Through thousands of interviews, Precision and Tunnl found that economic pressures, more than ideology, are shaping masculinity today. Religion is also playing a major role in men’s lives, especially among Gen Z, Davis said, with many finding a sense of community in faith in addition to platforms like YouTube and various podcasts rather than more traditional media institutions.

FIRST IN PI — CAPITOL HILL CELEBRATES JENNER & BLOCK: Congressional Republicans and Democrats came together last night for a bipartisan event celebrating the release of “ When Congress Comes Calling ,” a newly updated handbook on congressional investigations published by Jenner & Block and the Project on Government Oversight .

— Speaker Mike Johnson (R-La.) and Rep. Jim Jordan (R-Ohio), two of the president’s staunchest allies on Capitol Hill, were part of the crowd at the event, which celebrated the work of the government watchdog group and a law firm President Donald Trump previously accused of abusing its pro-bono practice to “engage in activities that undermine justice and the interests of the United States.”

— Jenner is one of four law firms that sued the Trump administration earlier this year in response to executive orders threatening their ability to do business. The order targeting Jenner accused the firm of engaging in “obvious partisan representations to achieve political ends.” It cited its previous hiring of former federal prosecutor Andrew Weissmann as justification for suspending security clearances held by firm lawyers, reviewing government contracts held by the firm and its clients and l

— But you wouldn’t detect any of that from the tenor of last night’s event, which brought Johnson and Jordan together with Democrats like Sen. Cory Booker (D-N.J.) and Reps. Zoe Lofgren (D-Calif.), Ro Khanna (D-Calif.) and Mary Gay Scanlon (D-Pa.), per a tipster.

— “This edition of ‘When Congress Comes Calling’ will serve as a go-to guide for congressional investigators for years to come, and we’d like to thank the Project on Government Oversight for entrusting us with the responsibility of updating this seminal publication,” said Ashley Callen , co-chair of Jenner’s congressional investigations practice.

SILICON VALLEY’S DATA CENTER PROBLEM: “Tech companies and lobbyists are investing millions of dollars to tackle a new political problem for the industry : Data centers, the lifeblood of the growing AI economy, are becoming toxic with voters,” POLITICO ’s Gabby Miller writes.

Y COMBINATOR FORMS A PAC: Silicon Valley startup accelerator Y Combinator has taken another step to bolster Little Tech’s political maturation in Washington with the launch of its corporate PAC. The new PAC, which is also referred to in FEC filings as Little Tech PAC, comes as the startup community has sought to compete with more entrenched Big Tech interests to shape AI and competition policy in Washington.

— It also follows the launch of a network of super PACs focused specifically on AI policy. One group, Leading the Future , said it has already reached $100 million in commitments from the likes of venture capitalists Marc Andreessen and Ron Conway , OpenAI co-founder Greg Brockman and Palantir co-founder Joe Lonsdale . The super PAC will pour that money into midterm races to support candidates that align with the industry’s AI priorities and to defeat candidates who oppose tough AI regulations.

— The clash centers on whether crypto exchanges should be allowed to pay an annual percentage yield via rewards programs to customers who hold stablecoins. — The issue “demands immediate action from every bank leader in the country,” ABA President Rob Nichols wrote in a letter to CEOs . “We need you — along with your staff and, where appropriate, your customers — to contact Congress and make our voices heard.”

A coalition of crypto companies led by the Blockchain Association wrote in a letter to senators last month that proposals to crack down on exchanges’ rewards programs “would reopen a settled issue, undermine a carefully negotiated compromise, reduce consumer choice, suppress competition, and inject uncertainty into the implementation of a new law before regulations have even been proposed.”

— Hemp, which only contains trace amounts of THC, was legalized due the 2018 farm bill. But a loophole allowing intoxicating hemp was closed last year after Sen. Mitch McConnell (R-Ky.) led an effort to include language banning intoxicating hemp products in the continuing resolution that ended the last government shutdown. That ban didn’t take immediate effect, but hemp farmers say they need to know now if crops that are currently legal will still be legal come harvest time.

— During a Thursday morning press conference, Rep. James Comer (R-Ky.) called the proposed two-year extension “the number one priority” to help the hemp industry. Asked if he had spoken to fellow Kentuckian McConnell about the proposal, Comer acknowledged their differing opinions on hemp, but said he was confident the two-year extension could pass the Senate if attached to a funding bill.
SINEMA SUED: Former U.S. Sen. Kyrsten Sinema is being sued for allegations of having an affair with a married man under an obscure North Carolina law.

— The former Arizona senator, and current senior adviser at Hogan Lovells , is accused of entering into a physical and emotional relationship with Matthew Ammel , a member of her personal security detail. Ammel and his family live in North Carolina — one of only six states with an “alienation of affection” law that allows a spouse to sue the third party in the case of infidelity.

— His spokesperson said Johnson’s more of a Johnny-come-lately on the issue. “Colin Allred never traded a single stock while serving in Congress — not because anyone required it, but because he believes public service demands putting the people’s interests ahead of personal gain,” Sandhya Raghavan said in a statement. “Meanwhile, Julie Johnson has actively traded stocks throughout her six years in the Texas Legislature and continued to do so as a member of Congress.”

— But Johnson, who was a successful small business owner and attorney before entering Congress last year, only fully started divesting her holdings in September after a bipartisan group of House lawmakers, including Reps. Alexandria Ocasio-Cortez (D-N.Y.) and Chip Roy (R-Texas), introduced the Restore Trust in Congress Act , which would ban congressional stock trading. Ocasio-Cortez recently endorsed Johnson .

— Johnson also gained attention last spring for making dozens of stock sales the day before President Donald Trump ’s tariff “Liberation Day” which sent stock markets temporarily reeling. Her office didn’t respond to questions at the time about the sales.

— What Whatley didn’t mention is that he and his family have up to a million plus dollars invested in three major oil companies that saw spikes in their shares after President Donald Trump said he would increase oil production in Venezuela, according to his personal financial disclosure filed in late November.

— Whatley, a former energy lobbyist , and his immediate family own between $321,000 and $890,000 in stock in Chevron , which is the only American oil major operating in Venezuela. CRITICAL LOBBYING : Ramping up critical minerals production in the U.S. involves a heady cocktail of domestic permitting reform, international infrastructure development and price floors — and that’s where lobbying giant Brownstein Hyatt Farber Schreck is stepping in.

— Brownstein’s new critical minerals practice, reported first in PI, will be led by co-chairs former foreign service officer Samantha Carl-Yoder and Obama alum Jason Buckner . The firm already has a significant number of critical mineral clients, but the formalization of the practice will enable more specialization for what the industry could need, Carl-Yoder told your host in an interview.

— Ballard signed the new client on Feb. 9, according to the disclosure, nearly three weeks after the U.S. International Trade Commission issued a final determination finding Stiiizy had imported vapes that infringe on patents held by domestic vape manufacturer PAX Labs . — As PI reported last year , Tesla lost several members of its public policy staff and cut ties with multiple outside lobbying firms amid Musk’s political realignment and vociferous support for then-candidate Trump. Tesla’s September 2024 signing of Akin Gump Strauss Hauer & Feld was an early sign that the company was seeking to reenergize its lobbying efforts but the firm appears to have done little work for Tesla since then, reporting no activity in 2025.
